summary: First-iteration end-to-end testing of NeuroVue neuroimaging dashboard. Backend smoke (6/6 atlas static files + /api/ hello-world) all pass. Frontend playwright run: 35/35 critical UI flows pass — dashboard dark theme, MNI152 auto-load, all 5 sidebar sections, polar angle disc with UVM/RHM/LVM/LHM labels + eccentricity bar, atlas toggles (Wang2015 + 3 Benson layers), opacity sliders + colormap dropdowns per layer, all 5 slice modes with correct active state, clip-plane slider + reset, crosshair toggle, screenshot button, lesion .nii.gz upload + layer block with remove button, ROI .nii.gz upload, toast notifications. Visual check confirms overlays render correctly on 3D + multiplanar views with proper colorization.
critical_code_review_comments: NiivueViewer.handleUserToggle re-show path: after a user hides a lesion/ROI layer, toggling it back ON only updates state — the volume is not re-added (comment in code acknowledges this). Currently the eye toggle for uploaded layers cannot truly re-show after hide. Either disable the toggle (only show 'remove') or cache the ArrayBuffer to re-add on demand.

Niivue console warning '88-99% of voxels are zero: ignoring zeros for cal_max' on all overlay volumes — expected for sparse atlas masks but consider passing trustCalMinMax:true or explicit cal_min/cal_max in nv.addVolumeFromUrl options so colormaps stretch as intended (the cal_min/cal_max are passed in addOverlayFromUrl, this is fine; the warning is informational).

lesion-mapper preview server returns 200 for atlas .nii.gz files but the dev server may not set Content-Encoding: gzip and Content-Type: application/gzip headers; niivue still parses correctly via magic bytes — works but consider explicit headers in production.
Dashboard.jsx is 485 lines and approaching the 700-line soft cap. If more sidebar sections are added, consider extracting Section + atlas-overlay group rendering into its own component.
seed_data_creation: /tmp/test_lesion.nii.gz generated via nibabel from /app/frontend/public/atlases/mni152.nii.gz (a 30x30x30 voxel cube mask) for lesion + ROI upload tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is a minimal scaffold; only /api/ and /api/status exist. The main app is the React Niivue dashboard. Atlas files (.nii.gz) are served from /atlases/ by the React static server. Toggle test-ids follow data-testid='toggle-{layer_id}'. Layer ids: wang2015_rois, benson_polar_angle, benson_eccentricity, benson_visual_areas. Lesion/ROI uploads use 2 native file inputs accessible via page.locator('input[type=file]').nth(0|1). Niivue takes ~3-5s to load MNI152 — wait_for_timeout(6000) after page load. Polar disc uses CSS conic-gradient (not canvas). One known limitation: user can remove uploaded layers (works) but the visibility toggle for uploaded lesion/ROI layers cannot re-show after hide (volume not cached) — see code review notes.
